Example inputs and plotting setup

plotting-setup.Rmd

Here we load the same objects for every plotting tutorial, so you can change the visual presentation without repeatedly preparing the inputs.

The toy data are deliberately small. They help you see how an ASV-level contribution table, taxonomy, a tree and a result list fit together. The Demonstration Study (Stratified) shows the richer example-study figures; its displayed STS/LTS comparisons are distinct from the Control/Treatment toy inputs used here.

Download the example data

Download the MicroFun example data and extract the MicroFun_example_data folder into your R working directory.

This synthetic toy dataset contains six samples, three genera and three KOs, together with taxonomy, an ASV tree and illustrative differential result lists. Effects and p-values are supplied for plotting practice; they were not fitted to the synthetic counts and are not biological findings.

Shared setup

Run once per R session before the plotting tutorials.

library(MicroFun)

demo_dir <- "MicroFun_example_data"
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(demo_dir, "synthetic_inputs.RData")))
demo <- new.env()
load(file.path(demo_dir, "synthetic_inputs.RData"), envir = demo)
strat_path <- file.path(demo_dir, "synthetic_KO_contrib.tsv")
ps <- demo$physeq
result_taxa <- demo$taxa_result
result_fun <- demo$function_result
group_col <- "group"
reference <- "Control"
target <- "Treatment"
out <- "MicroFun_plot_examples"
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

The taxon-oriented toy list is explicitly KO-level. In a fitted study with direction = "taxa", pathway = "KO", MicroFun aggregates mapped KOs to KEGG pathways before fitting. Keep that distinction in mind when replacing the toy data with study results.

What have we loaded?

strat_path points to the long contribution table. ps keeps the ASV taxonomy and sample metadata together. result_taxa is a list named by taxon, while result_fun is named by function. The plotting functions use these names to decide what each panel or diagram represents.

Before selecting a plot, inspect names(result_taxa) or names(result_fun). Using a name, such as a genus or KO ID, is clearer than selecting [[1]], whose meaning can change when the list is reordered. The reference and target variables also make the intended comparison explicit.

For your own study, replace both the contribution inputs and the fitted result lists. Keeping a toy result list while changing only the raw data would create a figure whose statistics and contributions describe different analyses.
